purpose: Contract for transparent, unit-safe, reviewable manufacturing calculations before calculation skills are authored.
output_invariants: Normalized units are shown before arithmetic when conversion occurs.
Every variable has a name, unit, and stated meaning.
The formula is named and shown before the result.
Intermediate values needed to review the result are visible.
Raw and rounded results are separate when rounding changes the value.
Missing, invalid, zero-denominator, contradictory, stale, or outlier inputs are visible.
A review owner or handoff is present when status is not CALCULATED.
The result does not claim legal compliance, engineering adequacy, certification, permit approval, or operational authorization.

temperature.rule: Temperature conversion requires an offset-aware conversion; never multiply C or F by a scale alone.

rules: Preserve original units and values in the output.
Normalize only within a declared dimension.
Reject incompatible dimensions and unknown units.
Do not silently convert count, mass, volume, length, time, currency, or temperature without the required conversion data.
Show the conversion factor and normalized value when inputs use different units.
Use exact arithmetic or sufficient precision for intermediate values.
Round only the final value unless a formula explicitly requires stepwise rounding.
Countable outputs use an explicit operational rule such as ceiling, floor, nearest whole, increment, or order multiple.
Rates, percentages, ratios, costs per unit, and durations retain fractional values unless a local policy says otherwise.
Report raw and rounded values whenever rounding changes the result.

required_checks: rounding policy missing for countable result
validation_contract.failure_behavior: Do not force a final numeric result. Return valid partial calculations, name the failed check, preserve the supplied evidence, and show the review handoff.
validation_contract.zero_denominator_behavior: Use NOT_APPLICABLE or REVIEW_REQUIRED with an explanation; never return infinity, zero, or an invented denominator.

reference_formulas.purpose: Time available per unit of required demand.

variables.name: available_production_time
variables.meaning: Net time available for the demand window after declared planned exclusions.

variables.name: required_demand
variables.meaning: Required output in the same demand window.

assumptions: The time window for available production time and demand is the same.
Planned exclusions are declared and not silently removed.
edge_cases: A negative or unavailable time is INVALID_INPUT.

reference_formulas.purpose: Theoretical output from available time and cycle time before losses or quality effects.

variables.name: available_production_time
variables.meaning: Declared production time.

variables.name: cycle_time
variables.meaning: Time per unit at the stated process condition.

assumptions: Cycle time is representative of the stated process condition.
The result is theoretical and excludes downtime, speed loss, and scrap unless separately applied.
edge_cases: Cycle time of zero or less is INVALID_INPUT.

reference_formulas.purpose: Combined availability, performance, and quality ratio for a declared period and asset/process boundary.

variables.name: planned_production_time
variables.meaning: Planned production time in the period.

variables.name: run_time
variables.meaning: Operating time in the period.

variables.name: ideal_cycle_time
variables.meaning: Ideal time per unit for the process.

variables.name: total_count
variables.meaning: All units produced in the period.

variables.name: good_count
variables.meaning: Units meeting the declared quality definition.

assumptions: All counts and times describe the same asset, process, and period.
Ideal cycle time is approved or supplied evidence.
Good count and total count use the same counting boundary.
edge_cases: Planned time, run time, or total count of zero requires NOT_APPLICABLE or REVIEW_REQUIRED.
Run time greater than planned time is contradictory unless explicitly explained.

reference_formulas.purpose: Share of units that pass the operation without rework on the first pass.

variables.name: first_pass_good_count
variables.meaning: Units accepted without rework at the operation.

variables.name: units_entering_operation
variables.meaning: Units presented to the operation.

assumptions: Reworked units are excluded from first-pass good count.
The numerator cannot exceed the denominator.
edge_cases: Units entering of zero is NOT_APPLICABLE.
Numerator greater than denominator is INVALID_INPUT.

reference_formulas.purpose: Share of started units recorded as scrap for a declared boundary and period.

variables.name: scrap_count
variables.meaning: Units classified as scrap under the declared disposition rule.

variables.name: units_started
variables.meaning: Units entering the declared production boundary.

assumptions: The production boundary and disposition rule are explicit.
Rework is not counted as scrap unless the disposition rule says so.
edge_cases: Units started of zero is NOT_APPLICABLE.
Scrap count greater than units started is INVALID_INPUT.

reference_formulas.purpose: Mean operating time between recorded failures for a declared asset and period.

variables.name: operating_time
variables.meaning: Time the asset was available for operation under the declared measurement rule.

variables.name: failure_count
variables.meaning: Count of failures included by the declared failure definition.

assumptions: Failure definition and observation window are explicit.
Operating time excludes intervals outside the declared measurement boundary.
edge_cases: Failure count of zero is NOT_APPLICABLE for a finite MTBF; report the observation window separately.

reference_formulas.purpose: Mean corrective repair time per recorded failure for a declared asset and period.

variables.name: corrective_repair_time
variables.meaning: Time spent on corrective repair under the declared start and stop rule.

variables.name: failure_count
variables.meaning: Failures receiving corrective repair in the observation window.

assumptions: The repair-time boundary is explicit and consistent across events.
edge_cases: Failure count of zero is NOT_APPLICABLE for a finite MTTR.

reference_formulas.purpose: Potential process capability relative to specification width using within-process variation.

variables.name: upper_spec_limit
variables.meaning: Upper customer or engineering specification limit.

variables.name: lower_spec_limit
variables.meaning: Lower customer or engineering specification limit.

variables.name: within_sigma
variables.meaning: Within-subgroup standard deviation from the declared method.

assumptions: The process is stable enough for a capability interpretation.
Specification limits are requirements, not control limits.
Within-subgroup sigma method and subgrouping are recorded.
edge_cases: Within sigma of zero or less is INVALID_INPUT or REVIEW_REQUIRED.
Unstable process evidence requires REVIEW_REQUIRED before capability interpretation.

reference_formulas.purpose: Centered process capability relative to specification limits using within-process variation.
reference_formulas.formula: cpk = min((upper_spec_limit - mean) / (3 * within_sigma), (mean - lower_spec_limit) / (3 * within_sigma))

variables.name: upper_spec_limit
variables.meaning: Upper specification limit.

variables.name: lower_spec_limit
variables.meaning: Lower specification limit.

variables.name: mean
variables.meaning: Process mean for the declared period and population.

variables.name: within_sigma
variables.meaning: Within-subgroup standard deviation.

assumptions: The process stability, subgrouping, and sigma method are recorded.
Specification limits are not inferred from the observed sample.
edge_cases: Within sigma of zero or less, reversed limits, or unstable evidence blocks interpretation.

reference_formulas.purpose: Three-sigma control limits for an X-bar subgroup chart using a declared center and within-subgroup sigma.
reference_formulas.formula: ucl = center_line + 3 * within_sigma / sqrt(subgroup_size); lcl = center_line - 3 * within_sigma / sqrt(subgroup_size)

variables.name: center_line
variables.meaning: Declared process center line.

variables.name: within_sigma
variables.meaning: Within-subgroup standard deviation.

variables.name: subgroup_size
variables.meaning: Number of observations per subgroup.

assumptions: The chart type, subgrouping, sigma method, and center-line period are recorded.
Control limits are not specification limits and do not by themselves prove process capability.
edge_cases: Subgroup size of zero or less is INVALID_INPUT.
Missing or unstable baseline requires REVIEW_REQUIRED.

rules: Raw and rounded values remain distinguishable

safety_boundary: Calculations are planning or analysis support. They do not authorize production release, maintenance, restart, engineering signoff, legal compliance, certification, permits, purchasing, staffing, or customer commitments.
